paper.title: Bayesian Optimization of CVaR with Unknown Hyperparameters

settings.name_in_paper: CVaR Bayesian optimization with unknown GP hyperparameters (finite candidate set)
unmapped: Objective is the CVaR_alpha over an environmental variable W ~ P_W of f(x,W); the learner queries pairs (x,w) and regret is measured on CVaR of the chosen design x_t
The learner knows the environmental distribution P_W (finite set of scenarios)
The kernel/hyperparameters are unknown; the learner knows a finite candidate set Theta of GP models containing a well-specified one (f in RKHS of k_theta* with norm <= B)
settings.definition_quote: We consider an unknown objective function $f : \mathcal{X} \times \mathcal{W} \to \mathbb{R}$ ... at iteration $t$ it actively selects a query $(x_t,w_t) \in \mathcal{X} \times \mathcal{W}$ and observes a noisy evaluation $y_t = f(x_t,w_t) + \varepsilon_t, \varepsilon_t \sim \mathcal{N}(0,\sigma_\varepsilon^2)$. ... cumulative regret $R_T := \sum_{t=1}^T r_t$ with per-round regret $r_t := \mathrm{CVaR}_\alpha[f(x_t,W)] - \mathrm{CVaR}_\alpha[f(x^\star,W)]$.

symbols.n_Theta: size |Theta| of the finite candidate set of GP models
symbols.beta_T: max_theta beta_T^theta, beta_t^theta = B + sigma_eps sqrt(2(gamma_{t-1}^theta + 1 + ln(2/delta)))

conditions: f in RKHS of k_{theta*} with norm <= B for some theta* in Theta
k_theta <= 1 for all theta in Theta
gamma_T is the max over theta of the maximum information gain
regret is cumulative CVaR_alpha regret: sum_t CVaR_alpha[f(x_t,W)] - CVaR_alpha[f(x*,W)]
tuning: xi_t = 2 sigma_eps^2 log(4|Theta| pi^2 t^2/(3 delta))

source.label: thm:regret
source.quote: Assume $f \in \mathcal{H}_{k_{\theta^\star}}$ with $\|f\|_{\mathcal{H}_{k_{\theta^\star}}} \le B$ for some $\theta^\star \in \Theta$, $\varepsilon_t \sim \mathcal{N}(0,\sigma_\varepsilon^2)$ i.i.d., and $k_\theta \le 1$ for all $\theta \in \Theta$. Set $\beta_t^\theta = ...$ and $\xi_t = ...$. Then with probability at least $1 - \delta$, the cumulative regret satisfies $R_T \le \mathcal{O}(|\Theta| B + |\Theta|\sqrt{\xi_T T} + \beta_T|\Theta|\sqrt{T\gamma_T})$

results.notes: Quantity set to 'other' since regret is on the CVaR risk functional. B mapped to S (RKHS norm bound). Restated identically as Theorem 5 in the appendix (not recorded separately). Sublinear when gamma_T = o(sqrt T).
